A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 21-page versions of the same MeCo paper. Their text, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original language-model training, downstream evaluation, toxicity measurements, and ablation results in Sections 3-5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the appendix experiments, variance analysis, and full benchmark tables.

M1.justification: The metadata-conditioning and cooldown procedure, loss masking, attention handling, model architectures, and conditional inference remain unchanged. Newly documented sequence length and document-boundary tokens do not establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same C4, RefinedWeb, and DCLM training data, ten downstream benchmarks, and conditional-generation/toxicity scenarios. Newly cited Ukrainian-language research is not an added experiment.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains standard pre-training, fastText data selection, and the additional-80B-token reference. The comparator membership in conditional-inference and ablation experiments also remains unchanged; new citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training budgets, evaluation sampling, five-shot and zero-shot procedures, and toxicity-generation settings are unchanged. Appendix A supplies previously unstated sequence-length and token-boundary details without reporting a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The same metadata-mixing, URL-variant, frequency, hashing, topic, cross-document-attention, and cooldown-length analyses remain in Section 5 and Appendix B. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report single full pre-training runs and the same Appendix B.2 variance check: three continuations from a common 90% baseline checkpoint using disjoint data. Table 13's standard-deviation reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Performance values, toxicity findings, and appendix result entries are unchanged; Table 1 still reports averages of 55.7 for standard training and 56.7 for MeCo. Table 5's added 42% and 65% labels round the 41.6% and 65.1% coverage figures already stated in v1's Section 5.2.

T1.justification: The metadata definition and mathematical content are unchanged. Neither version contains a formal theoretical development or proofs, and v2's expanded discussion of prior research introduces none.

C1.justification: The claims of 33% less training data, gains across model scales and corpora, conditional steerability, and metadata flexibility remain unchanged. The introduction's added emphasis on realistic training clarifies the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 retains the same hypotheses about source prioritization and structured representations. The limitations concerning English-only experiments, single runs, unstudied post-training interactions, and uncertain mechanisms are unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 6 newly specifies packing sequences to 8192 tokens, and Appendix A.2 newly states that each document receives BOS and EOS tokens. These improve implementation documentation; hardware, training-time information, prompts, and the code/model/data access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds Kyrylov and Chaplynskyi (2023), Weller et al. (2024), and Wettig et al. (2025). Sections 1 and 6 expand acknowledgment of Allen-Zhu and Li's synthetic experiments, and the related-work discussion adds a connection to domain taxonomies while retaining the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction's prior-work paragraph is rewritten, Section 6 receives focused expansions, and Appendix A gains brief clarifications. The title, section order, and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 removes the misleading '#Parameters' label from its corpus comparison. Table 5 adds coverage annotations and Table 6 adds a sequence-length row, accompanied by local reflow. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility through the previously missing sequence-length and document-boundary specifications, expands relevant research context, and clarifies figure and table labels. These useful corrections preserve the existing methods, empirical evidence, and limitations, producing a limited overall quality improvement.
